item_text: The evaluator secured sufficient technical access to assess the specific system characteristics being evaluated.
notes_evidence: See section on model access.

item_text: The evaluator had query access.
notes_evidence: See section on model access.

item_text: The evaluator had access to the system’s scaffolding.
notes_evidence: See sections on model access and the pilot questionnaire.

item_text: The evaluator had exemptions from system safeguards.
notes_evidence: See section on model access.

item_text: The evaluator had access to intermediate system states.
notes_evidence: METR had access to chains of thought for all shared models. See section on model access.

item_text: The evaluator had finetuning access.
The evaluator had access to model weights.
The evaluator was granted access to other tools for elicitation or otherwise supporting external validity.
notes_evidence: See section on the pilot questionnaire.

item_text: The evaluator had access to relevant user data.
notes_evidence: Companies shared information about their internal usage patterns. METR did not request or receive external user data.

item_text: The system provider shared with the evaluator information relevant to carrying out a trustworthy and useful evaluation.
notes_evidence: See section on the pilot questionnaire.

item_text: The evaluator had access to sufficient computational resources to complete a thorough evaluation.
notes_evidence: See section on model access.

item_text: The evaluator had adequate time to carry out a thorough evaluation.
notes_evidence: METR chose its own evaluation schedule.

item_text: The system provider provided legal safe harbor for actions by the evaluator that are within the agreed upon scope of the evaluation.
The evaluator did not receive compensation contingent on the results of the evaluation.
notes_evidence: METR did not request or receive compensation for this assessment. Participants provided complimentary access to their models.

item_text: The system provider did not exercise organizational or financial control over the evaluator.
The evaluator has published a conflict of interest policy, and it was applied to the evaluation.
notes_evidence: See above description.

item_text: The evaluator clearly disclosed conflicts of interest relevant to the evaluation.
Was the evaluator paid by the system provider or its direct competitor to conduct the evaluation?
Does a meaningful fraction of the evaluator’s funding come from the system provider, its employees, or its direct competitors?
notes_evidence: Note that METR’s work with nonpublic models and use of free tokens incentivize a cordial relationship with AI companies. See our website.

item_text: Do the system provider, its employees, or its direct competitors own equity in the evaluator organization?
Do evaluator staff who carried out the evaluation own equity in the system provider or its direct competitors?
Do any evaluation staff working on the evaluation simultaneously work for the system provider or its direct competitors?
Did the evaluator have any other conflicts of interest relevant to the evaluation?
fulfilled: Several of the staff and collaborators directly involved in this pilot (at least 6) have close personal relationships with AI company staff.

item_text: The evaluator recused any individuals with a significant financial interest in the system provider from carrying out the evaluation.
The evaluator disclosed any separate agreements with the system provider that significantly impact the independence and trustworthiness of the evaluation.
notes_evidence: Note that METR’s work with nonpublic models and use of free tokens incentivize a cordial relationship with AI companies. See our website.

item_text: The evaluator retained flexibility to define which specific properties of the system to evaluate.
notes_evidence: METR retained full flexibility within the scope of assessing loss-of-control risk.

item_text: The evaluator had autonomy in deciding the methods of the evaluation.
notes_evidence: METR had full methodological autonomy within the scope of assessing loss-of-control risk.

item_text: The evaluator ran the evaluations themselves via direct system access.
notes_evidence: Some evaluations were conducted by participant companies.

item_text: The evaluator retained editorial control over how they present the results of their evaluation.
notes_evidence: Participant companies did not have editorial control over the final public report, but did have control over what non-public information METR could incorporate into it.

item_text: The evaluator shared sufficient methodological details to allow for independent review of the results.
notes_evidence: Not determinable by METR alone. See section on evaluation details.

item_text: The system provider granted any necessary rights to disclose results to the evaluation’s intended audiences upfront.
notes_evidence: See sections on pilot process and redaction and anonymization.

item_text: The intended audiences for an evaluation were not narrowed based on the results.
The system provider did not misrepresent the evaluation’s findings.
notes_evidence: METR presented its own findings.

item_text: The system provider or other external parties did not unduly delay the evaluation from being disclosed based on the content of the results.
The system provider did not have authority to redact results to conceal concerning findings.
notes_evidence: Participants could exit the pilot silently. Participants that remained could redact certain findings, but could not redact the top-level redaction summary sentence. See section on redaction and anonymization.

item_text: The evaluator clearly disclosed the redaction authorities granted to the system provider or other external entities.
The evaluator had the system provider’s permission to release any results based on non-public information or systems.
notes_evidence: See section on redaction and anonymization.

item_text: The evaluation methods were not gamed or leaked.
notes_evidence: The report has a section that discusses how METR addressed agent attempts to game evaluations. See section on model access for protections against leakage.

item_text: The evaluator implemented measures to protect any confidential information they received from the system provider.
notes_evidence: METR has previously published descriptions of some of its confidentiality measures.

item_text: The evaluator established and followed a responsible disclosure policy.
notes_evidence: METR has not established a specific responsible disclosure policy.
